_comment: Guided tour for the Trace Browser emtk app. Steps point at real controls (spec attr / action names, or the names the app registers); steps with an await wait for the user and are released by their outcome: setup_accepted (the browser page is shown), folder_opened (files are listed), several_selected (more than one file selected), exported (an export, delete or hand-off finished).

steps.title: What this does
steps.text: The Trace Browser lists the TTTR files of a folder, draws the intensity trace of the file you select and keeps a rating and a note for every file. The tour covers the setup, opening a folder, the options, the table, the trace, notes, selecting, exporting, deleting, the hand-offs and help.

steps.title: Accept a detector setup
steps.text: The setup page says which routing channels and micro-time windows make which trace, and the file type. Choose a setup in the editor and press Continue. When a setup was used before the app already shows the browser page and this step is done.

await.hint: Press Continue on the setup page to open the browser.

steps.title: Open a folder
steps.text: Press Open and choose a folder with TTTR files, or drop a folder on the window. The files are listed in the table and the first one is plotted.

await.hint: Press Open and choose a folder with TTTR files.

steps.title: Subfolders and the rating filter
steps.text: Include subfolders also lists the files of nested folders (the .trash folder is never listed). Filter shows only the files with a rating of at least 1, 2 or 3 stars, or only the unrated ones.

steps.title: Bin window and y range
steps.text: Bin window [ms] is the width of a time bin; changing it loads the trace of the selected file again. Y min and Y max set the y axis of the trace plot; equal values fit the data.

steps.title: The file table
steps.text: Click a row to select a file. Double click a Rating cell (0 to 3) or a Notes cell to edit it, then press Enter. Ratings and notes are saved beside the data in the folder.

steps.title: The trace
steps.text: One line per detector of the setup plus their sum; the histogram on the right counts how many bins hold each count. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, double click to fit. A trace that is empty usually means the setup does not match the file.

steps.title: Write an annotation
steps.text: The Annotation box holds free text about the shown file. It is the same text as the Notes cell and is saved shortly after you stop typing.

steps.title: Select several files
steps.text: Export, CSV, DOCX, Delete and the hand-offs work on the selected files. Press Select all to select every listed file; click a row to go back to one file.

await.hint: Press Select all to select every listed file.

steps.title: Export what you selected
steps.text: Export copies the selected files into a folder you choose. CSV writes each selected trace (time and one column per series) at the current bin window. DOCX writes a Word report into the opened folder and needs the python-docx package.

await.hint: Press Export or CSV and choose a folder.

steps.title: Delete is a move
steps.text: Delete asks first, then moves the selected files and the files that share their name to the .trash folder of the opened folder. Nothing is deleted for good. Do not press it now unless you mean it.

steps.title: Open the trace in another tool
steps.text: HMM, TW and NDX open the first selected file in a new Intensity Trace Analysis window, a new TTTR Time Window tool and a new ndX window, with the current bin window. They work inside ChiSurf and are greyed when the Trace Browser runs on its own.

steps.title: Help
steps.text: Help explains every part of the window and links to the documentation page with a worked example. Guide starts this tour again.
